newsitem.title: USA: NGC sees Q1 gain on its Belvieu stake sale.
newsitem.headline: NGC sees Q1 gain on its Belvieu stake sale.

text.p: NGC Corp said on Friday that it would post a gain in the 1997 first quarter because its Warren NGL Inc unit agreed to sell its 80 percent ownership interest in a Texas factionation facility to Koch Hydrocarbon Co.

The natural gas and gas liquids marketer had agreed to divest its stake in the Mont Belvieu I facility to obtain Federal Trade Commission consent to close its merger with Chevron Corp's midstream businesses.
NGC said the sale would be effective January 1, 1997 and was subject to Federal Trade Commission approval.
The company was not immediately available to comment on the possible size of the gain.
The Mont Belvieu I facility had a capacity of about 110,000 barrels per day, the company said.
"This sale completes the most significant obligation under our agreement with the Federal Trade Commission," Steve Furbacher, president of Warren and senior vice president of NGC, said.

"After the sale, we will continue to have a strong presence in Mont Belvieu through our ownership of the Warren Mont Belvieu fractionator, which we acquired through the Chevron merger, and our 38.75 percent interest in the Gulf Coast Fractionators facility," he said.
